risks: model ranking does not hold across windows
series is close to noise; fitted weights would overfit
diagnosis.narrative: The series carries a strong long-run trend. Seasonality is strong (period 52): a repeating cycle explains much of the movement. The spectrum is close to white noise, so most of the variation is irregular and hard to predict. The series reads as stationary by the ADF/KPSS tests. A few outliers stand out (3 points, ~3% of the sample). Across validation windows the model ranking is unstable (Kendall tau 0.127), which favours a robust combination.

Test a per-horizon weighted mean with softmax_neg_error on the full pool to capture potential horizon‑specific strength differences.
The series has strong trend/seasonality but unstable rankings; a simple mean over the full pool may provide a robust baseline and test a different aggregation type.
The series has unstable ranking and strong seasonality; a robust median over all models may outperform mean/trimmed.
Try a robust DBA combination on the full pool to see if iterative optimization improves over trimmed mean, given unstable ranking.
The ranking is unstable and we have a per‑horizon top‑k mean handle (w3). Testing a per‑horizon weighted mean should explore a different combination type.
Try a forward-selection weighted combo over the full pool to capture complementary models when ranking is unstable.
The series has unstable rankings and strong seasonality; a robust weighted combo on the reduced pool may improve over the trimmed mean.
Test a robust weighted combination on the smaller stable pool (pool4) using inverse-error weights to see if a simpler, more stable pool improves over the softmax version.
The leader is a trimmed mean on pool4; a simple mean over the same robust subset may be competitive given the unstable ranking hint.

decision.justification: Selected 'trimmed_mean on pool4' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.8625. Series context: trend strength 1.0 and seasonal strength 1.0; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau 0.127); 2 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 0.351.
